title: Story file
description: A reading text, used both by the Library reader and by a lesson's story section. A paragraph is normally all target-language text, tappable and resolved through the dictionary at read time — EXCEPT a paragraph carrying its own `lang` different from the course (see the paragraph definition's `lang` property), which renders as plain, non-tappable, non-spoken text instead. Hungarian's A1 unit stories use this deliberately: narration is English scaffolding for a true beginner, dialogue is Hungarian; no Spanish story uses it as of this writing. NOTE: paragraphs currently come in two shapes across the library (see the paragraph definition). Only the typed shape renders speaker labels; 49 of 50 stories use the untyped shape and therefore render entirely as narration.

id.description: Also the read-state key, so it must be unique across the library and stable — changing it makes a finished story look unread. Two conventions are in use: 49 files use the bare filename ('a2-classics-01') and one uses a dotted form ('story.a1.01'). The dotted form is preferred for new files; the difference is cosmetic because the manifest passes whatever it finds straight through.

level.description: Decides which reading room the story appears in.

lesson.description: Lesson number this story belongs with, if any.

type.description: Informational only — the manifest takes the shelf from the directory the story sits in, never from this field, so the two cannot disagree in the UI. Note the classics shelf is spelled 'classics' as a directory but 'classic' inside all ten of its files; both are accepted here.

category.description: Legacy alias for type, present in one file. Prefer type.

source.description: Classics only: where the text came from.

text.description: Fallback for a story with no paragraphs. The reader renders it as a single narration block.

paragraph.description: A paragraph renders as dialogue only when type is exactly 'dialogue'; anything else, including a missing type, renders as narration. Authoring a conversation without type/speaker loses the speaker labels.

type.description: Omitted in 49 of 50 existing files, which is why their dialogue reads as narration.

speaker.description: Required for dialogue; ignored otherwise. Should appear in characters.

id.description: Present in most files, read by nothing. Harmless.

lang.description: Overrides the course language for THIS paragraph only. Omit for ordinary (monolingual) target-language text — every existing story before Hungarian's A1 Unit 1 relies on the default. When present and different from the course, the reader renders plain escaped text: no tap-to-translate (an English 'a' would otherwise resolve against the Hungarian dictionary and show 'the'), no text-to-speech (which would otherwise read English narration in the target-language voice).
